subject: Urgent: LiveBridge stream failures impacting latency & error rate
messages:
From: Samir Khan <skhan@livebridge.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@livebridge.com
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: (no subject) — stream errors after SDK upgrade

Ben —

We've got a production incident hitting ~30% request error rate and a ~200ms median latency increase on our streaming endpoints since we rolled the LiveBridge client SDK 1.3.2 last night. Errors are HTTP 500s coming out of Redwood's streaming gateway; our SRE pulled a few traces and they look like the stream parser is mis-parsing headers when multiple frames arrive back-to-back.

Symptoms we see:
- Intermittent "malformed headers" entries in nginx + Redwood gateway logs around the same timestamps as the 500s.
- The client SDK appears to coalesce small header blocks into one frame under higher throughput which in turn triggers a parser assertion in the Redwood SDK integration (we can reproduce in staging).
- Rolling back our fleet to SDK 1.3.1 reduces errors back to normal within 10 minutes.

Attaching a trimmed trace + a screenshot of the gateway error log. We need a quick triage call and an action plan — this is affecting two production tenants and one internal timeout pipeline. Can you loop in engineering and ops? We'll be available for a short bridge now or anytime this afternoon (PDT).

Attachments: lb_trace_0822.json, screenshot_stream_error.png

Thanks,
Samir Khan

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Re: stream errors after SDK upgrade (technical notes)

Looping in technical details from my quick triage: we reproduced the failure in a small staging harness by simulating increased concurrent streams from the LiveBridge client 1.3.2. The root cause appears to be a mismatch in how the SDK batches header frames versus how our streaming parser expects frame delimiter semantics.

Key log snippets (sanitized):
[2028-08-22T16:05:18Z] client=10.12.4.9 level=error stream_parser.go:142 parse_error: "unexpected token in header block"
[2028-08-22T16:05:18Z] gateway=redwood-gw-03 level=warn gateway_handler.go:88 got 502 from downstream, raw_bytes: "GET /v1/stream\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nX-LiveBridge-Client: 1.3.2\r\n\r\nPOST /v1/stream\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n"

What happened: when small header frames arrive in quick succession the client concatenates them in a single TCP segment without an explicit inter-frame sentinel. Our parser was written with the assumption that each header block arrives as a distinct logical unit; the concatenation leads to the parser consuming bytes across logical boundaries and throwing a malformed-header error.

Short-term mitigations we can push immediately (ETA: 1–3 hours):
- On Redwood gateway: make the parser tolerant by scanning for repeated HTTP start-lines and splitting concatenated blocks (risk: small perf hit).
- On LiveBridge side: force a 1ms Nagle-like spacing between header writes or disable header coalescing in SDK 1.3.2 (risk: slightly higher outbound packet rate).

Next steps (ETA):
- I'll prepare a minimal server-side patch to detect and split coalesced header blocks (PR + canary within 48 hours).
- Coordinate with LiveBridge to roll client rollback or client-side mitigation immediately.

Attachments: proposed_patch.diff (sent privately to eng mailing list)

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Subject: RE: Urgent: LiveBridge stream failures impacting latency & error rate

Samir — thanks for staying on this. Per our triage: Karthik confirmed a header-coalescing/stream-boundary mismatch between the LB client 1.3.2 and Redwood's streaming parser. We discussed three immediate actions and a short timeline below.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
1) Mitigation (now): We recommend that you either roll back to client SDK 1.3.1 (fastest) or enable the client-side non-coalescing flag for 1.3.2. Redwood will also deploy a parser-tolerance fix to staging to reduce customer impact while we validate the patch.
2) Patch (48 hours): Redwood will open a server-side patch to detect & split concatenated header blocks and ship a canary by EOD + full rollout after verification.
3) Postmortem (72 hours): Joint RCA doc and timeline; Redwood will include regression guard in our integration tests to prevent re-introduction.

Proposed customer communication (you can copy/paste):
"LiveBridge and Redwood teams have identified a compatibility issue between LiveBridge client SDK 1.3.2 and Redwood's streaming parser that can cause intermittent stream parsing errors under high throughput. We recommend rolling back to SDK 1.3.1 or applying the advised client-side mitigation while Redwood pushes a server-side hardening patch. Redwood estimates a canary within 48 hours and a full remediation rollout shortly after. Our teams will coordinate status updates on the bridge and provide a joint postmortem."

If rollback is acceptable we can help coordinate the rollback and monitor error rates as soon as it's live. If you'd prefer Redwood to land the patch to staging, grant us permission and we'll proceed.

I've attached a short mitigation plan and the Zoom link for the bridge.

Attachments: redwood-mitigation-plan.pdf

Thanks — Ben
